title: A Person or Place That Matters to Me

opts: чьё влияние я до сих пор ощущаю
prepTasks.correct: чьё влияние я до сих пор ощущаю

writingModel: The Person Who Changed How I Read — by Kamila Seitkali

There is a woman who changed my entire approach to books — and I have never met her. Her name was Apai Zarina, an elderly Kazakh librarian who worked at WKU for thirty-seven years. I discovered her through the handwritten notes that she left in the margins of dozens of library books — notes which were not summaries but responses, not repetitions but arguments.

Her notes were remarkable. In one ancient, yellowed linguistics textbook, she had written: "The author has not read Saussure carefully enough." In a beautiful old Central Asian history book, she had noted that one paragraph contradicted another source entirely. These were the observations of someone who read with great concentration and no deference to authority — a reader whose attention was total.

What she gave me was a way of reading that I had never considered. I had always read passively — receiving information from texts without replying. Zarina's notes showed me a different kind of reading: reading as conversation. Since discovering her, I have started writing responses in the margins of my own books — not summaries, but my honest reactions. Disagree. Question. Connect. Reply.

The place that connects me most to Zarina is, of course, the WKU library — specifically, the fourth floor, where the oldest books are kept. It is a quiet, slightly dusty place that smells of old paper. When I sit there and open one of those books, I sometimes wonder if she sat in the same chair, at the same worn wooden table, reading by the same low winter light.

Zarina never knew she was teaching me. She probably never knew anyone was reading her notes. But the influence which she had on my life is one of the most significant I have experienced. She is the person who showed me that paying attention is itself a form of generosity — that when you read carefully and respond honestly, you give something to the world, even if no one is watching.
A person who teaches you something important doesn't always know they're doing it. And the place that matters most isn't always the one you chose — sometimes it chooses you.

writingTemplate.suffix: — and I will never forget them/it.
writingTemplate.hint: Open with a relative clause: "a person WHO..." / "a place WHERE..."
